_README.what: Hand-written local names for gazetteer entries. The human half of the gazetteer.
why_a_separate_file: dhaka_central.json is generated by scripts/harvest_gazetteer.py and is overwritten
on every re-harvest. This file is never generated, so the hand work survives.
Keys are entry ids from dhaka_central.json; the loader merges them at read time
and logs a warning for any id it cannot find, because a typo'd id means aliases
why_this_cannot_be_automated: Fuzzy matching fixes spellings. Aliases fix synonyms. OpenStreetMap spells the
Mirpur 10 roundabout গোলচক্কর (golchokkor); much of Dhaka says গোলচত্বর
(golchattar). Those are different words for one place and share almost no
letters, so no edit distance reaches one from the other. This file is the
difference between the search working and not working, and it is also exactly
what a general-purpose map cannot do for Dhaka.
_README.convention: An entry listed here counts as reviewed: a person read it and supplied its local names.
note_on_scope: Only entries a demo or a judge is likely to type are listed. The other ~5,900
harvested entries resolve on their own OSM names and are marked reviewed: false.
That is honest rather than complete. Extending this file is the work that B7
maintenance_after_a_re_harvest: An alias can be made redundant, and then harmful, by a later harvest. If a newly
harvested entry carries as its OWN name a string listed here as somebody else's
alias, two entries match that query exactly, so resolve() refuses as ambiguous and
the lookup stops working. The loader logs a warning naming both entries, and
The fix is to DELETE the alias, not to rename anything: the harvested entry bears
the name itself and is almost always the better answer. S31 removed five on exactly
these grounds, and each query became more precise as a result --
'Mohakhali flyover' now resolves to the 250 m flyover instead of the 1,200 m
Mohakhali area, and 'Sayedabad bus terminal' to the 300 m terminal 70 m away
instead of the 1,200 m Saydabad area.
